t: Latin, the language of Latium and Rome, spread with Roman power across the western Mediterranean and became the language of law, government and a great literature from Cicero and Virgil onwards.
Spoken Latin changed region by region into the Romance languages, among them Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian and Romanian, now the first languages of nearly 900 million people.
Written Latin outlived the Roman Empire by more than a thousand years as the language of the Church, the universities, science and diplomacy in Europe.
dyk: Latin remained the official language of the Kingdom of Hungary until 1844, when the Hungarian diet made Hungarian the language of government in its place.
ev: The earliest Latin inscriptions, among them the Lapis Niger in the Roman Forum
Livius Andronicus stages the first Latin play adapted from a Greek original
The golden age of Latin literature: Cicero, Caesar, Lucretius, Virgil and Horace
Jerome translates the Bible into Latin: the Vulgate
The Council of Tours orders sermons to be preached in the “rustic Roman tongue” or in German
The Oaths of Strasbourg, the earliest surviving text in an early form of French
Isaac Newton publishes his Principia in Latin
The Second Vatican Council opens the way to the Mass in the languages of the people

f.script: The Latin alphabet, adapted from an Etruscan form of the Greek alphabet
f.earliest: Inscriptions of the 6th century BCE, among them the Lapis Niger in the Roman Forum and the Duenos vase
f.status: No native speakers; the official language of the Holy See, taught in schools and used in the Catholic liturgy, law and science
